title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The previous page recalls that, for a smooth complex curve X, the transcendental construction from uniformization (the projective structure induced by the universal covering, Fuchsian when X is hyperbolic) gives a canonical projective connection on X. This is a canonical analytic section of the torsor P_{X/C} of projective connections, which is a torsor under H^0(ω^{⊗2}). Grothendieck asks when this connection is 'logarithmic', i.e. has regular singularities at infinity, as a connection on the associated P^1-bundle P(I/I^3).

This page.
(1) Conjecture. 'Regular singular at infinity' should mean the following. The section extends over the smooth compactification X̂ (a section of P_{X̂/C}) and has at most simple poles along X̂−X.
(2) Indeterminacy group. Let D be the reduced divisor X̂−X. Two such connections then differ by an element of H^0(X̂, ω^{⊗2}(D)): quadratic differentials with at most simple poles at the punctures.
(3) Computing this group. Write λ = ω^{⊗2}_{X̂/C}. Tensor 0→O→O(D)→O(D)/O→0 with λ. Since O(D)=J_D^{-1} and O(D)/O ≅ (J_D/J_D^2)^{-1} ≅ ω^{-1}|D (normal = tangent at a point of a curve), one gets λ(D)/λ ≅ (λ⊗ω^{-1})|D = ω|D. This gives the cohomology sequence 0→H^0(λ)→H^0(λ(D))→H^0(D, ω|D)→H^1(λ).
(4) Case g ≥ 2, X connected. By Serre duality H^1(λ) is dual to H^0(ω^{-1}) = 0. So there is a short exact sequence 0→H^0(X̂,ω^2)→H^0(X,ω^2)^{reg}→⊕_{p∈D} T*_p X̂→0, of ranks 3g−3, 3g−3+ν, ν.
(5) Moduli interpretation. Grothendieck identifies this with the cotangent sequence at the point ξ of the forgetful map M_{g,ν}→M_g: H^0(ω^2) = Ω^1_{M_g}(ξ), H^0(ω^2(D)) = Ω^1_{M_{g,ν}}(ξ) (with a self-query 'car?'), and the quotient is the cotangent space of the fibre (the moving punctures).
(6) Consequence. The canonical uniformizing projective connections of a family of punctured curves thus form a (non-holomorphic) section of an affine bundle over M_{g,ν} modelled on Ω^1_{M_{g,ν}}.

Next page. The cases g = 0, 1 bring in Lie Aut(X̂), vector fields vanishing on D, and a correction term Q(X).

Purpose. This belongs to the study of Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs and of projective connections (opers / indigenous bundles), presumably with an eye on the char-p Cartier operation in the same dossier.
errors: Imprecision in the pole condition. Relative to a holomorphic projective structure on X̂, the Fuchsian (uniformizing) projective connection at a cusp has a DOUBLE pole: the Schwarzian of the local uniformizer gives 1/(2z^2) + c/z + ... . What is true is the following. A regular-singular (logarithmic) connection on the P^1-bundle corresponds to a quadratic pole. Two such connections with the same leading coefficient (unipotent monodromy, exponent difference 0) differ by a quadratic differential with at most simple poles. So H^0(ω^2(D)) is the right indeterminacy group only for the torsor of projective connections with prescribed cusp leading term, not for 'connections with at most simple poles' literally. Grothendieck's 'sauf erreur' flags his own uncertainty.

The identification H^0(X̂, ω^2(D)) ≅ Ω^1_{M_{g,ν}}(ξ) is correct by Kodaira–Spencer, since T M_{g,ν} = H^1(X̂, T(−D)) is Serre dual to H^0(ω^2(D)). Grothendieck's 'car?' is just a self-query, not an error. Strictly it is the cotangent of the moduli stack, or of the coarse space at curves without automorphisms.

ideas.what: Canonical uniformizing projective connection on a punctured curve, viewed as a section of the torsor of projective connections, with regular (logarithmic) singularities at the punctures
ideas.modern_name: Fuchsian projective structure / indigenous bundle (oper) with log poles at marked points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Poincaré, Klein; accessory parameters). Algebraic formulation: Gunning (1967), Mochizuki (1996, p-adic Teichmüller theory), Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as far as known; possibly echoes in the Cartier-operation/Gauss–Manin material of this dossier

ideas.what: Exact sequence 0→H^0(ω^2)→H^0(ω^2(D))→H^0(D, ω|D)→0 for g≥2 via residue of quadratic differentials (λ(D)/λ ≅ ω|D)
ideas.modern_name: Cotangent sequence of the forgetful map M_{g,n}→M_g via Kodaira–Spencer / Serre duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard deformation theory (Kodaira–Spencer; Ahlfors–Bers for Teichmüller spaces)

ideas.what: The space of regular-singular projective connections over M_{g,ν} is an affine bundle (torsor) under Ω^1_{M_{g,ν}}, and the uniformization gives a canonical C^∞ section
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of projective structures / indigenous bundles over moduli; accessory parameters as a 1-form on moduli
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning, Kra, Hubbard (1981); Zograf–Takhtajan (1987: d-bar of this section gives the Weil–Petersson form); Mochizuki (1996)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the canonical uniformizing projective connection of punctured curves as a section of a torsor under the cotangent bundle of M_{g,ν}. This is exactly the starting point of the 'accessory parameters as a 1-form on moduli' picture. He does not pursue the natural next step, computing d or d-bar of this section, which by Zograf–Takhtajan (1987) yields the Weil–Petersson form and Liouville action. The page shows him identifying the right algebraic framework (log-pole projective connections, torsor under Ω^1_{M_{g,ν}}) in a dossier also concerned with the Cartier operation. This anticipates the algebro-geometric framing later made systematic by Mochizuki's indigenous bundles on pointed curves.
missed.quote: on aura comme groupe d'indétermination des conn. proj. sing. rég. à l'infini sur X̂ H^0(X̂, ω^{⊗2}(D)) ... H^0(X,ω^2)^reg ≃ (car?) Ω^1_{M_{g,ν}/C}(ξ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority rather than new mathematics. It documents Grothendieck (dossier dated c. 1972–81) treating uniformization as a section of the torsor of (log) projective connections over M_{g,n}, adjacent to Cartier/p-curvature material. That is a link between complex uniformization and the later p-adic/char-p theory of indigenous bundles that is not usually traced to him.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is standard: Serre duality and the Kodaira–Spencer cotangent sequence. The interest is historical, in Grothendieck framing uniformization as a section of a torsor of regular-singular projective connections over M_{g,ν}, prefiguring Zograf–Takhtajan and Mochizuki. But the page itself stops at routine identifications.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: likely 'est en fait défini sur X̂, compactifiée non singulière canonique de X, i.e. sont P_{X̂/C}' rather than 'a un sens défini sur X̂, compactifiée sans singularité contenant X ... C_{X̂/C}'. The torsor letter is probably the script P of the previous page.
Indeterminacy line: likely 'groupe d'indétermination des conn. proj. sing. rég. à l'infini sur X̂', not 'groupe d'indéterminées des conn. quasi-sing.'.
The quotient in (a) should read H^0(D, ω|D) consistently, with marginal note 'rang ν = card D'. The 'rang 3g−3' annotation refers to H^0(X̂, ω^2) = Ω^1_{M_g}(ξ).
Bottom notes: 'M_g variété modulaire des courbes de genre g complètes'; 'M_{g,ν} variété modulaire pour courbes à ν trous'.
